englishTransition: Let me begin with why I wanted to make this robot open source.

title: When a companion's service ends
zh: 当陪伴机器人的服务停止时
lines: Change a case. Make an outfit.
notes:
Stack-chan is a palm-sized, open-source robot with two motors and a simple face. People change a case to fit a motor they already own, or make outfits and comics. Today I want to show how those small acts changed the community—and changed me.

A communication robot can become a companion. When its proprietary service ends, that companion can die while its body is still beside you. I wanted people to repair their robots, replace services, and keep them running. I wanted a community where everyone could be both a developer and a user. First, let me show how I learned to build this robot.

title: Learning to build a robot
notes: Around 2018, I shared face-animation software for M5Stack. I wanted to give that small face a moving body. After joining a robotics startup, I learned mechanical design, circuits, and embedded software. I tried those skills in my spare time and gradually built my own robot. JavaScript was familiar, so the Moddable SDK helped me approach embedded development through a language I knew. This personal project grew while I was learning.
side:
Around 2018: a face
Learning as I built

title: The birth of Stack-chan
notes: This is the tweet where I shared Stack-chan in my hand. The name Stack-chan combines M5Stack with “chan,” an affectionate Japanese suffix. With a battery inside, it could move without a power cable. I wrote that it had become a real robot I could hold on my palm. The first version was rough, but that small face now had a moving body. This was before I knew what other people would make with it.
label:
M5Stack + chan
an affectionate suffix

title: A paper-tube octopus
notes: To explain why simple creations matter so much to me, let me share a small memory from kindergarten. We made things for an exhibition about sea creatures. Other children used lots of boxes and paper. I made an octopus from one paper tube. My teacher asked me to make something more elaborate, so I made a second octopus. The teacher still wasn't satisfied, and I felt sad. But I was attached to my simple octopus. That memory stays with me when I think about making robots. Complexity and attachment are different things. A simple creation can mean a lot to its maker. I want people to be able to show what they made with pride, even when it is small or unfinished. That feeling is part of why I made Stack-chan simple.

title: Two motors and a simple face
zh: 两个电机，一张简单的脸
lines:
Two motors are enough
to begin
notes: I don't want robot making to be a privilege reserved for experts. Connect two motors to a microcontroller, give it a simple face, and you already have a robot. A small movement can make that face feel alive. It doesn't have to be complicated to become something you care about. More advanced experiments are welcome, and the two-motor version can remain a starting point. People can learn by building and changing it, with help where they need it. Then other makers began adapting it to their own needs.

title: An existing maker community
zh: 从已有的创客社区出发
side:
M5Stack
Shared projects
People helping people
notes: This circle shows other makers, alongside personal making. The circles show overlapping ways in, not the order people joined. I already belonged to a maker community around M5Stack, a compact module with a screen. Makers shared projects and advice, and distributors such as Switch Science helped make the hardware available. I learned from their work. Some became Stack-chan's first builders. The rough first version took effort to assemble. Sharing the design was a start; people willing to try it and help made it useful.

stageDirections.text: Point from the central robot to the wider ring. Pause for 2 seconds.

title: A case for a different motor
zh: 为不同的电机改造外壳
notes: An early contribution came from tomorrow56, who had a different motor available. They modified the case to fit an SG-90 servo, used the parts they had, and shared the result. Participation began with one person's circumstances: a part they already owned and a change they wanted to make. Their version gave the next builder another option.

title: Other boards are welcome
notes: I welcomed other boards from an early stage: Arduino, obniz, and other ARM-based boards. M5Stack was my starting point, while other people brought tools and knowledge they already liked. The photograph shows the variety at a maker event. These versions came from their experiments, beyond anything I had planned. Different hardware could belong to the same project. Sharing a name raised another question.

title: Keeping the shared name available
zh: 让共同的名字持续可用
lines: A shared name for makers and companies
notes:
Registering a trademark might sound like a bit much for a personal hobby. But the name had become something we shared. As the original creator, I wanted the name to stay open across different hardware, including M5Stack's. I wanted individual makers and companies to share it, rather than tie it to one manufacturer's products.

Please check the published guidelines for the conditions that apply, and ask if your use is unclear. Code licenses and the shared name each have their own rules. The trademark came before the derivative-work guidelines.
label: Use conditions: published guidelines

stageDirections.text: Indicate the published-guidelines label. Pause for 2 seconds.

title: Takao's kits
side:
Making it easier
to begin together
notes: Takao prepared and distributed kits and organized gatherings where people worked on their robots together. Delivering kits reliably and helping with assembly take sustained effort. A kit made assembly easier; a gathering offered somewhere to ask for help. He provided support I could never have delivered alone. Personal projects and hardware adaptations continued alongside it. I was learning from what other people contributed. Some people took part in ways I had never expected.

title: Many kinds of making
side:
Stack-san by Latte
Comics and outfits too
notes: This circle adds more ways to create. This is Stack-san, a wearable creation by Latte. Its scale and the way it meets people are very different from my desk robot. Beside it is a four-panel comic by sylacwa. Other people make outfits or tell stories about their Stack-chans. I hadn't anticipated these forms of participation. On Twitter, I noticed people whose interests were different from the engineering circles I knew. They were enjoying the same character through their own kinds of making. Engineering remained important, with more ways to take part alongside it.

stageDirections.text: Point to the new creative activities, leaving the earlier rings visible. Pause for 2 seconds.

title: Your feedback keeps me making
zh: 你的反馈让我继续创作
notes: When someone shares a photo of their Stack-chan, I want to work on it again the next weekend. When they tell me where they got stuck, I know which documentation to improve. That keeps me making.
label: Photos and questions help me improve

title: Guidelines and a place to ask
zh: 创作指南与交流的空间
notes: The derivative-work guidelines came later, to support free use and reduce uncertainty. The code, name, and other people's photographs each have their own rules. People also need somewhere to ask practical questions. On Discord, they can show work in progress and discuss a motor, an expression, or an outfit. They may meet someone who has tried something similar. I support that space by watching what people are doing and helping them continue. The community's activities guide what I do next.

title: A role you can name yourself
zh: 自己定义在社区中的角色
notes: I made a business-card editor that anyone can use. People can name their own way of taking part and introduce the role they want in the community. The card makes that self-introduction visible when people meet. It can start a conversation about what someone likes making. I want people to have that freedom to name their role, alongside the freedom to change the hardware or software.

title: A robot's birthday party
notes: At a birthday party, these different activities meet. People bring robots, outfits, and stories about their attempts. A technical achievement and a first attempt can both be worth sharing. They meet people they may later ask for help, or help themselves. I discover work that happened without me. The relationships and knowledge people share give them more ways to continue. Long-standing makers also opened new entrances through AI.

title: AI Stack-chan
zh: 社区带来了 AI 对话
side:
robo8080
An early maker opens new entrances
notes: An existing maker opened another entrance through AI. robo8080 was already part of the M5Stack community and was exploring AI in 2022. Later, he connected Stack-chan to an LLM and created AI Stack-chan. Other people shared tutorials and further integrations. An experienced member's experiments opened an entrance for people who had never built a robot. They could start with an interest in AI and meet a physical robot they could change. Personal making, hardware adaptations, and creative expression continued alongside it. A ready-made product offers another way to begin.
sources: Speaker's clarification: M5Stack-era participation and AI activity in 2022, October 2026

stageDirections.text: Point to the AI entrance while keeping the earlier activities in view. Pause for 2 seconds.

title: M5StackChan brings new people
side:
A ready-made robot
A physical place for AI
notes: M5Stack introduced the commercial M5StackChan, with very little involvement from me. I welcome this ready-made way to begin, especially for people interested in trying AI in something physical. They can meet makers interested in hardware, outfits, and other activities. Community AI experiments and this product add different possibilities. People can still build the original robot or change a case. Those new possibilities also change what I want to make next.

title: Growing with the community
lines: A person can listen, then join
notes:
The dotted outside circle is open for what comes next.

As the community grew, my role changed too: manuals, a trademark, guidelines, communication tools, and business cards. I learned to respond to what people needed. Growing Together means this too: the members grew, the community grew, and I grew with them.

I want to try several Stack-chans talking together, with a person listening and joining when something interests them. Which robot speaks next? Where does it look? How does it notice someone wants to join? Blinking, gaze, small movements, and pauses still matter, even with two motors. This is an experiment I want to explore, rather than a finished system I am showing today.

stageDirections.text: Point to the dotted outside ring. Pause for 2 seconds.
Turn from the diagram to the audience. Pause for 2 seconds after “I grew with them.”

title: 10 minutes to begin, 10 years to keep making
zh: 十分钟开始，十年持续创作
lines: A future goal, not today's headcount
Five years old: curious, playful, still making
notes:
I have two long-term goals.

One is a robot you can start developing in ten minutes and keep making with for ten years.

The other is a community of ten thousand people around the world. That is a goal for the future, not our current headcount.

Stack-chan is five years old, halfway through that ten-year horizon. Five is an age for curiosity, play, and making friends. I want the next five years to leave room for adventures we haven't imagined yet.

The community can be a safe base: somewhere to ask for help, share an unfinished attempt, and return after something fails. That support can make it easier to try something new.
sources: Speaker's approved goals and closing, October 2026

title: Come and join us
lines:
A safe base for
new adventures
notes:
Come and join us. You can build your own robot or begin with an M5StackChan, then bring something you enjoy making. You can program, draw a comic, make an outfit, share a photo, or tell us where you got stuck. I want the community to be a safe base that welcomes experiments and mistakes. From there, we can go out and try our own adventures. You can make something ambitious, or enjoy a small two-motor robot at your own pace.

We are growing together: the makers, the community, and me. Today, being here is my small adventure. Thank you.

stageDirections.text: Look toward the audience. Pause for 2 seconds after “the makers, the community, and me.”
